analysis:
Integration pass over a docs, diagnostics and counter PR. Changed behavior: (1) a new optional `DaemonState.Stats.cancellationsPartialComplete` (DaemonStateFile.swift, head ~133-145; nil default, so older state files decode), populated in ProviderLoop+Trust.swift:70 from `stats.cancellationsPartialComplete`. (2) New `Status.servedRequestLines` (StatusCommand+ServedRequests.swift:10-24), called from StatusCommand.swift:175, which prints served count, output tokens and daemon uptime, and adds an 'ended early ... may be unpaid' line when the count is positive. (3) Reworded DoctorRunner.swift messages at lines 223 and 241. (4) Doc, changelog and test updates (cli-reference.md ~1020-1031, troubleshooting.md lines 87 and 144, DoctorOperatorDiagnosisTests).

Security assessment: all new data is an aggregate counter or label in the local owner-scoped daemon-state.json and in terminal output. It carries no prompt content, keys, tokens or machine identifiers, so A-001, A-003, A-008 and A-010 are untouched. No change to the WebSocket protocol (TB-002), App Attest authorization (TB-011, T-052/T-053), the attestation chain (TB-009), the prefix cache (T-041), the fan helper, or the add-on hold socket (TB-012). The helper makes no network calls, spawns no processes and parses no untrusted input. The wording is more accurate: it says counts are daemon-session-scoped, output-token-only and not authoritative for payment, which reduces overclaiming (T-056) and does not change billing controls.

Unverified contracts (not findings): the definition and increment site of `stats.cancellationsPartialComplete`, the cancel and drop path semantics (T-010), and the platform `cumulativeDelta` and payment claims are outside the supplied evidence. Integration replay was partial (43 units omitted). Those questions concern correctness and documentation accuracy, not a demonstrated security regression. Any path that sends this counter to the coordinator or to billing would need its own review, but this diff does not show one.
